title_as_printed: Experimental dew points for {xH2O+(1-x)CH4} giving the dew point temperature Td, the dew point pressure pd, and the corresponding amount-of-substance density rho_d of the saturated vapour for various amount-of-substance fractions x of H2O. The uncertainties dTd in Td, dpd in pd and drho_d in rho_d are also listed
pressure_note: dew-point pressure pd of the mixture (absolute), from the intersection of polynomial fits of the isochoric (p,T) data on the two-phase and single-phase sides

value.what: overall H2O mole fraction of the mixture charged = water mole fraction of the saturated vapour at its dew point (Td, pd)

value2.what: amount-of-substance density of the saturated vapour at the dew point, from the break point of fits to (pressure, density) on both sides (two-phase side uses a pseudo-density, overall mass / volume)

notes: Dew points are located by the authors from the discontinuity in slope of the measured isochoric (p,T) curve: fifth-order polynomial on the two-phase side, fourth-order on the vapour side, intersection = (pd, Td); uncertainties from the statistical uncertainty of the fit parameters. Composition x is known from the charged masses (no separate uncertainty given). The authors compare Td with Peng-Robinson (dij 0.399): maximum deviation about 3.7 K at the lowest water content. Dew-point water content here is at 427-596 K and 7.4-22.5 MPa.
